source_title: Lost mettle! VAML, Vedanta, Nalco sink up to 6% as metal index drops 3% - Business Standard
source_excerpt: Metal stocks remained under pressure for the fourth consecutive session on Friday amid broad-based selling in the markets. As of 11:55 AM, the Nifty Metal index was down 3.5 per cent, making it the worst-performing sectoral index. All 15 constituents of the index were trading in the red. Vedanta Aluminium Metal led the losses, falling 6 per cent to ₹338, followed by National Aluminium Company (Nalco), which declined 4.6 per cent to ₹296.70. Vedanta Ltd, Hindustan Copper and Hindustan Zinc slipped 4-4.5 per cent to trade at ₹224.90, ₹395.10 and ₹496.45, respectively. Other stocks, including Tata Steel, Steel Authority of India (SAIL), NMDC, Jindal Stainless, Jindal Steel, APL Apollo Tubes and Lloyds Metals and Energy, also traded lower, falling by up to 4 per cent. The latest decline has dragged the Nifty Metal index down around 6.3 per cent over the past four trading sessions, compared with a 3 per cent fall in the benchmark Nifty 50 index in the same period. At current levels, the Nifty Metal index is down around 18 per cent from its record high of 13,931.35, touched on June 15, 2026. Why are metal stocks falling? Analysts said that metal stocks are under pressure amid global economic uncertainty, rising energy prices, and declining investor sentiment toward cyclical stocks. Brent crude prices spiking to $114 is a major negative for the economy and markets, raising inflation and freight-cost concerns. Piyush Jhunjhunwala, founder and CEO, Stockify, said that any rise in energy costs typically puts pressure on profit margins of the companies, especially for those that lack captive energy supply or pricing power. Steel, aluminium and copper prices are determined to a great extent by industrial production, infrastructure investment and demand for manufacturing, particularly in China, which is one of the biggest consumers of metals. "A slowdown in China or weakening of global manufacturing will impact commodity prices and earnings forecasts of Indian metal companies. The strong US dollar and high bond yields will put downward pressure on commodity prices and demand for cyclical stocks," he said, adding that companies that enjoy lower cost of production, with a manageable debt, may be in a better position to withstand the volatility. "The Nifty Metal Index is expected to remain volatile in the near term, with a cautious undertone following the recent correction. Weak global metal prices, uncertainty over Chinese demand and elevated input costs may constrain recovery, although resilient domestic infrastructure demand and stabilising commodity prices could offer support. A sustained rebound will depend on improving market sentiment and a recovery in heavyweight metal stocks," said market expert Supriya Madye.
